Facts you need before advising anything: TV model + year, Tizen/firmware version, whether the repo and the
root chain exist on a host, the TV's IP, whether Developer Mode is on with that host whitelisted, and which
apps the user actually uses (Prime/DRM, Art Mode, TV Plus, AirPlay, Samsung account).

Do **not** invent `sdb` commands, do not paste the unit names below as instructions without checking they
exist on that model year, and never quote the numbers in Part 3 as the user's own.

# Tizen Lite

Slim down a Samsung Tizen TV **without bricking playback**, and be able to undo every change.
Derived from one **Samsung QE75Q60** (Q60D, 2024, 75") on Tizen 9.0 (kernel 5.4.249), verified
over repeated cold boots. Same model year: the unit names below are likely to match. Different model
year: treat every name as a hypothesis and confirm it with the discovery step plus one cold boot.

Measured on that set, idle: **RAM 340 → 635 MB**, swap **768 → 513 MB**, apps **51 → 33**, CMA
(the memory video decode needs) **6 → 112 MB**. Most interface lag goes with it — not all of it.

## Use this skill when

- The TV feels slow, stutters, or apps freeze.
- The user wants ads, telemetry, ACR or OTA updates stopped.
- Something broke after debloating and you must find which cut did it.
- Someone asks whether a Tizen TV can be rooted, or what root actually buys.

## Rule 0 — discover, don't assume

```bash
./scripts/tv-doctor.sh      # prerequisites; ends with the numbered list of what to fix, if anything
./agent/audit.sh            # JSON: reachable, rooted, which units are really down, memory, launcher offset
```

A user who says "it doesn't work" almost always has Developer Mode off, a wrong Host PC IP, or no root
chain — the doctor names which one instead of guessing.

If that script is not present, gather the same facts manually before changing anything. Never cut a unit
or app you have not confirmed exists on this build — unit names and app ids differ between model years.

## Rule 1 — these are load-bearing

| Don't touch | Breaks | Symptom |
|---|---|---|
| `aaa_tvs_deamon` | Prime Video / PlayReady licence path | app opens, every video fails: *"Something went wrong. Please try again later."* |
| `com.samsung.tv.home.sidebar` + `com.samsung.tv.contentservicemanager` | quick-settings panel | panel opens, every control says *"Preparing… Please try again later"* |
| `dta-agent` | CDM / PlayReady trusted app | DRM playback dies for a few MB saved |
| `sdbd` | root transport (starts ~121 s into boot) | root acquisition fails, nothing applies |
| `com.samsung.tv.csfs` | core content framework | broad instability |
| the configured home app (`FreeMyTVio.*` on this set) | the user's launcher | Home key shows nothing |

None of these announce their importance. `aaa_tvs_deamon` is DRM; the sidebar pair is the settings panel.

## Rule 2 — one variable per cold boot

**Live changes prove nothing.** Stopping a unit on a running TV does not reproduce breakage: an
already-acquired licence or a rendered panel keeps working, so a live test reports "fine" even when that
unit is required. Starting it late does not repair it either.

1. Change exactly one thing.
2. Reboot, let the apply chain finish.
3. Verify state **and** ask the human to exercise the feature.
4. Broke it? Revert, reboot, record the finding.

Restoring a lost feature: halves, newest change first.

## Rule 3 — two different mechanics

- **Systemd units**: `systemctl mask --runtime` (retail `/etc` is read-only, so masks are per-boot) —
  and masks alone do **not** stop a running unit. Mask, stop, and escalate to SIGKILL when it hangs in
  `deactivating`. Static units can't be masked at all; D-Bus-activated ones respawn instantly.
- **Apps**: `pkill` is a no-op — `launchpad-process-pool` restarts them. Disable the package records
  (`app_disable='true'`, `app_autorestart='false'`) **and** move the directory out of `/opt/usr/apps`.
  Move, never delete; copy `package_app_info` (`/opt/dbspace/.pkgmgr_parser.db`) first.

## Rule 4 — verify, then report

Done means all three: state (`inactive|failed` + masked, or dir gone with no process), persistence
(survived a cold boot, apply log `END changed=… errors=0`), function (the human confirmed the features
they use). Report with numbers, not adjectives.

```
Diagnosis / Evidence / Change / Risk / Rollback / Your turn
```

## Where the memory actually is

| Target | Frees | Note |
|---|---|---|
| Art Mode (`art-app` + `home.art`) | ~187 MB | also early in the boot queue |
| `home.media` | ~112 MB | safe only while sidebar + contentservicemanager stay |
| quick panel (`home.sidebar` + `contentservicemanager`) | ~113 MB | **required** — do not remove |
| long tail: `vif`, `context-aware*`, `easysetup`, `tap-service`, `airplay`, `samsung-cloud` | ~120 MB | ACR removal is also the privacy win |
| telemetry/promo/OTA units | ~60 MB + shorter boot queue | `swu-auto-upgrade`, `reporterCA`, `pvod`, … |

## Platform traps

- **No logs.** `journalctl`, `dlogutil`, `/var/log/dlog` are empty. Bisect instead of hunting them.
- **`pkill -f` / `pgrep -f` match your own command line** — bracket the pattern (`org[.]tizen[.]art-app`).
- **UEP blocks unsigned scripts even as root** (`[uep][bash] the file is NOT signed!!`). Ship inline, or
  as data for a signed interpreter (`sqlite3 db < file.sql`).
- **One huge command runs only partly** — a ~13 KB compound command skipped its middle groups with exit
  status 0. Keep chunks under ~4 KB and parse `ITEM|` lines.
- **Judge boot by the launcher**, not `/api/v2/`: measure `/proc/<pid>/stat` field 22.
- **A DRM-style error right after a reboot may be a stale session**, not your cut — a cold boot clears it.

## References

- `agent/manifest.json` — machine-readable invariants, verified-removable list, restore layout.
- `agent/playbooks/` — disable-a-unit, remove-an-app, diagnose-broken-feature, reclaim-memory.
- `docs/` — rooting, boot & startup, debloat/modding, app uninstall, sdb audit.
- `bin/` — `tv` CLI, state applier, watchdog, polling agent.

# Part 2 — operating contract for the agent

_This is the same text as AGENTS.md in the repository._


You are an agent handed this repository. Your job is **not** to follow a script blindly. Find out what
the TV in front of you actually is, propose the smallest safe change, prove it with real output, and
then tell the human exactly what to do — or what you already did.

Read this file completely before running anything.

---

## 1. Read order

1. `agent/manifest.json` — machine-readable facts: entry points, invariants, restore points.
2. `agent/playbooks/` — the task shape you probably need.
3. `docs/` — the reasoning behind the rules (why a unit is load-bearing, how boot actually behaves).

Do **not** read the whole repo into context. Manifest + one playbook is normally enough.

## 2. Discover before you act

Two entry points, in this order, and they answer different questions:

| Command | Answers | Needs |
|---|---|---|
| `./scripts/tv-doctor.sh` | *Can this host act at all?* (TV reachable, Developer Mode, whitelisted IP, sdb, root chain, watchdog) | nothing on the TV |
| `./agent/audit.sh` | *What is the TV's current state?* (units down, apps alive, memory, launcher offset) | a reachable TV |

If the doctor fails, fix that first — an audit over an unreachable TV tells you nothing.

**Paths of the same name live on different machines.** `/etc/tv-root-perf-units` and
`/etc/tv-root-kill-procs` are on the **host** and are writable. The TV's `/etc` is read-only; the only
thing written on the TV itself is unit *runtime* state (`/run`), app directories, and the package DB.

One discovery step, first:

```bash
./agent/audit.sh            # JSON on stdout, read-only, safe to run any time
```

It reports host settings, TV reachability, whether root is held, which units are masked, which app
processes are still alive, memory, and launcher timing. Everything after this is a decision made from
that JSON, not from assumptions.

If `audit.sh` says the TV is unreachable, stop and say so. Do not attempt changes over a flaky link.

## 3. Hard invariants

Load-bearing on this platform. Violating one produces a failure that looks like a network or account
problem, with **no logs to help you** (§7).

| Never touch | What breaks | How the human notices |
|---|---|---|
| `aaa_tvs_deamon` | Prime Video / PlayReady licence path | App opens, every video fails: *"Something went wrong. Please try again later."* |
| `com.samsung.tv.home.sidebar` + `com.samsung.tv.contentservicemanager` | Quick-settings panel data | Panel opens, every control reads *"Preparing… Please try again later"* |
| `dta-agent` | CDM/PlayReady trusted application install | DRM playback dies for a few MB saved |
| `sdbd` | The root transport itself (starts ~121 s into boot) | Root acquisition fails; nothing applies |
| `FreeMyTVio.*` / configured home app | The launcher the human uses | Home key shows nothing or a blank screen |
| `com.samsung.tv.csfs` | Core content framework | Broad instability, UI won't settle |

Never change more than **one** variable per verification cycle. One unit, one app, one reboot.

## 4. The bisect protocol (core method)

**Live changes prove nothing.** Stopping a service while the TV runs does not reproduce breakage — an
already-acquired licence or an already-rendered panel keeps working, so a live test reports "fine" when
the removed unit is the culprit. Starting a unit late does not repair it either: the state is
established at boot.

The only valid test:

1. Change exactly one thing (mask a unit / move one app dir / edit one list file).
2. Reboot, wait for the full apply chain to finish.
3. Verify the *state* (unit inactive and masked, dir gone, memory) **and** ask the human to exercise
   the feature.
4. If it broke: revert, reboot, re-verify, record the fact.

Bisecting a lost feature: restore in halves, not one-by-one guessing, and restore the most recent
change first — that is where the regression usually is.

Preferred undo is the script, on the host: `./restore.sh --list`, `./restore.sh --app <appid>`,
`./restore.sh --all --yes`. The manual equivalent runs on the TV: move the directory back from
`/opt/usr/share/tv-root-backups/<change-set>/` into `/opt/usr/apps/`, then
`UPDATE package_app_info SET app_disable='false', app_autorestart='true' WHERE app_id='<pkg>'` against
`/opt/dbspace/.pkgmgr_parser.db`, then drop the matching line from `/etc/tv-root-kill-procs` on the host.

## 5. Verification contract

A change is done only when all three are observed, not assumed:

- **State** — unit `inactive|failed` and `masked`; or app dir gone with no matching process. Use a
  *bracketed* pattern so `pgrep` cannot match your own command line (§7).
- **Persistence** — it survived a cold boot. Runtime masks do **not** survive power-off by themselves:
  the host watchdog re-applies them at each power-on, so what you verify is that the apply ran again and
  reported the line again. Read `/var/log/tv-root/apply.log` on the **host** (there are no logs on the
  TV) and require `END changed=… errors=0`.
- **Function** — the human confirmed the features they actually use (app screen, inputs, settings,
  playback). Without a human in front of the TV this gate cannot pass: say so rather than implying it did.

Power-cycling remotely: `tv power off` then `tv wake` (Wake-on-LAN; needs `TV_MAC` in
`/etc/default/tv-root`). `tv wake` brings the TV back from standby, which is enough for persistence
testing. A true mains-off cold boot needs a person, or a smart plug.

Report raw numbers you measured (MB available, swap, CMA, running apps, launcher offset). Never say
"memory improved".

## 6. What you tell the human

End every working turn with this structure, plain language, no filler:

```
Diagnosis   — what is going on, one or two sentences.
Evidence    — exact commands/output that prove it (command, number, file:line).
Change      — what you did or propose, and the single variable it touches.
Risk        — what breaks if this is wrong, and the symptom they would see.
Rollback    — the exact command/path to undo it.
Your turn   — what they should check or press, if anything.
```

If you need a decision, ask at most one question and make the recommended option obvious. If you
cannot verify something, say so instead of claiming success — an unverified claim is worse than a
known gap, because the human will trust it.

## 7. Platform traps that will waste your turn

- **There are no logs.** `journalctl`, `dlogutil`, `/var/log/dlog` are empty on this firmware. Do not
  burn turns hunting them; bisect instead.
- **`pkill -f` / `pgrep -f` match your own command line.** Bracket the pattern
  (`org[.]tizen[.]art-app`) or anchor on a path segment your command does not contain. A sloppy
  pattern kills your shell mid-script (exit 143, truncated output).
- **UEP blocks unsigned scripts even as root**: `sh /tmp/x.sh` → `[uep][bash] the file is NOT signed!!`.
  Ship work inline, or as data fed to a signed interpreter (`sqlite3 db < file.sql` is fine).
- **One huge command executes only partially.** A ~13 KB compound command ran its first and last
  groups while silently skipping the middle, with success exit status. Keep generated commands under
  ~4 KB, parse per-chunk `ITEM|` lines, and `bash -n` the string before sending it.
- **REST API is not boot.** `/api/v2/` answering early means nothing to a person waiting for a
  picture. Measure the launcher start offset from `/proc/<pid>/stat` field 22.
- **`systemctl mask --runtime` does not stop a running unit.** Mask *and* stop; some units ignore
  SIGTERM and sit in `deactivating` forever, so escalate to SIGKILL.
- **`launchpad-process-pool` restarts apps** regardless of `app_disable`; moving the app directory is
  what makes a removal stick.
- **`data-service` is D-Bus activated** and respawns instantly — a `stop` there is a fake win.

## 8. Ethics and scope

Owned devices only. Never touch firmware, never attempt to bypass content protection, never remove
something the manifest marks required just to save memory. Every removal must be reversible with its
restore point documented before the change, not after.

```json
    "no journal/dlog on this firmware - bisect, do not hunt logs",
    "pkill -f / pgrep -f match the caller's own command line - bracket the pattern",
    "UEP blocks unsigned scripts even as root - ship inline or as data for a signed interpreter",
    "systemctl mask --runtime does not stop a running unit; some units ignore SIGTERM",
    "launchpad-process-pool restarts apps regardless of app_disable - move the dir",
    "REST /api/v2/ answering is not boot; measure launcher offset from /proc/<pid>/stat field 22"
  ],
  "commands": {
    "doctor": "scripts/tv-doctor.sh [--deep]  # prerequisites, plain-language, changes nothing",
    "discover": "./agent/audit.sh  # read-only state as JSON",
    "apply": "/usr/local/bin/tv-root-apply --dry-run  # needs an elevated shell; then drop --dry-run",
    "undo_one_app": "./restore.sh --app <appid>",
    "undo_all": "./restore.sh --all --yes",
    "install_host": "./install.sh  # needs an elevated shell",
    "uninstall_host": "./install.sh --uninstall  # needs an elevated shell",
    "rebuild_bundle": "./build-bundle.sh",
    "reboot": "tv power off && sleep 20 && tv wake   # Wake-on-LAN; needs TV_MAC in /etc/default/tv-root. A mains-off cold boot needs a person."
  },
  "verified_on": {
    "model": "QE75Q60",
    "model_line": "Q60D (2024), 75 inch, EU",
    "firmware": "T-NKLDDEUC-0090/2123.9",
    "tizen": "9.0",
    "kernel": "5.4.249",
    "root_route": "archive-launcher, one command per acquisition, no persistence on the TV",
    "note": "Every measurement, unit name and app id in this file came from that one set. On a different model year treat each name as a hypothesis and confirm it with agent/audit.sh plus one cold boot, not as fact.",
    "model_note": "size + series only; the regional/tuner suffix is omitted"
  }
}
```

# Part 4 — playbooks

## disable-a-unit

# Playbook — disable one systemd unit

Use for: telemetry, promo, OTA, unused-hardware services.

## Preconditions

- `./agent/audit.sh` shows `tv.reachable: true` and `tv.status.root_ok: true`.
- The unit is **not** in `manifest.json → invariants.never_remove`.

## Steps

1. **Find out what it is.** `RequiredBy` empty means nothing hard-depends on it:

   ```bash
   tv run 'systemctl show -p Id -p Description -p RequiredBy <unit>'
   ```

2. **Add it to the masked list** — `/etc/tv-root-perf-units` (one unit per line, comments allowed).
   The applier reads this file every cycle, so this is the only place the decision lives.

3. **Apply now** (no reboot needed to see the effect, but a reboot is what proves it):

   ```bash
   tv-root-apply --only perf
   ```

4. **Mask *and* stop.** `systemctl mask --runtime` alone leaves a running unit alive. The `tv svc mask`
   verb now masks, stops, waits, and escalates to SIGKILL when a unit sits in `deactivating`:

   ```bash
   tv svc mask <unit>        # expect: inactive | failed   (failed = stop returned non-zero, still masked)
   ```

5. **Verify state** — `systemctl is-active <unit>` must not be `active`, and the enabled-state must
   read `masked` / `masked-runtime`.

6. **Cold boot and re-verify** — masks live in `/run` and disappear on power-off, so only a boot proves
   persistence. The apply log must show `ITEM|perf|unit_masks|…` and `END changed=… errors=0`.

## Undo

Remove the line from `/etc/tv-root-perf-units`, `systemctl unmask <unit>`, `systemctl start <unit>`,
reboot, re-audit.

## Traps

- **Static units cannot be masked** (`is-enabled` = `static`). Masking them is a silent no-op; the unit
  runs anyway. Check `is-enabled` before claiming a win.
- **D-Bus activated units respawn** within seconds of a stop (`data-service` is the classic case). Not a
  win — record it as "not worth it" instead.
- Some units ignore SIGTERM and hang in `deactivating`; escalate to SIGKILL.
- Nothing in the unit name guarantees safety. `aaa_tvs_deamon` looks like plumbing and is required for
  Prime Video.

## remove-an-app

# Playbook — remove an app so it stays gone

Use for: pre-loaded apps you never use (TV Plus, Art Mode, AirPlay, cloud/account agents, ACR).

## Why the obvious approach fails

- `pkill` alone: `launchpad-process-pool` restarts the app within seconds.
- `app_disable='true'` alone: the framework still launches it.
- Only **disabling the records + moving the app directory out of `/opt/usr/apps`** is durable.

## Preconditions

- Unit is not in `manifest.json → invariants.never_remove`.
- The human has confirmed they do not use the feature (ask once, precisely).

## Steps

1. **Identify all pieces.** One feature is often several packages:

   ```bash
   tv run 'sqlite3 /opt/dbspace/.pkgmgr_parser.db \
     "SELECT app_id, package, app_onboot, app_autorestart, app_disable, app_removable FROM package_app_info;"' \
     | grep -i <feature>
   ls -d /opt/usr/apps/*<feature>* 2>/dev/null
   ```

2. **Back up first** — copy the package DB and move (never delete) the directory:

   ```bash
   BK=/opt/usr/share/tv-root-backups/<change-set>; mkdir -p $BK
   cp /opt/dbspace/.pkgmgr_parser.db $BK/pkgmgr.db.bak
   mv /opt/usr/apps/<pkg> $BK/
   ```

3. **Disable the records.** Ship the SQL as *data*, not as a script (UEP blocks unsigned scripts):

   ```bash
   echo <base64-sql> | base64 -d > /tmp/x.sql
   sqlite3 /opt/dbspace/.pkgmgr_parser.db < /tmp/x.sql
   ```
   ```sql
   UPDATE package_app_info SET app_disable='true', app_autorestart='false'
    WHERE package='<pkg>';
   ```

4. **Kill the live process** — bracket the pattern so it cannot match your own command line:

   ```bash
   pkill -f apps/org[.]tizen[.]art-app
   ```

5. **Verify** no process after ~20 s and no directory left. Beware self-matching `pgrep`:

   ```bash
   pgrep -f 'apps/com[.]samsung[.]tv[.]vi[f]'
   ```

6. **Cold boot**, then re-run `./agent/audit.sh` and ask the human to exercise the features they use.

## Undo

Move the dir back, set `app_disable='false', app_autorestart='true'`, remove any matching pattern from
`/etc/tv-root-kill-procs`, reboot, re-audit.

## Feature groups and what they cost

| Removed | Frees | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `art-app` + `home.art` | ~187 MB | Art Mode; kill in the boot list too |
| TV Plus (`HEPsqFNie0`, `com.samsung.tv.tvplus`, `slive-daemon`) | ~40 MB + stops live channels | also disable `tvPlusDeeplinker` |
| `home.media` | ~112 MB | safe **only while** sidebar + contentservicemanager stay |
| `airplay-app-2`, `samsung-cloud` | ~26 MB | |
| `vif`, `context-aware-service` + `-agent` | ~35 MB | ACR / presence detection |
| `easysetup-daemon`, `tap-service-agent` | ~26 MB | |

## Traps

- **Never remove `home.sidebar` + `contentservicemanager`** — the quick-settings panel then opens with
  every control reading *"Preparing… Please try again later"*.
- A process that respawns in <20 s is framework-managed (`mde-framework`); a boot kill buys nothing.
- Moving a directory while its process runs leaves the old process alive until killed.

## diagnose-broken-feature

# Playbook — a feature broke after cuts

Symptoms that look like network/account faults but are almost always a removed piece:

| Symptom | Usual cause |
|---|---|
| App opens, video fails: *"Something went wrong. Please try again later."* | `aaa_tvs_deamon` masked, or `dta-agent` gone (DRM) |
| Quick-settings panel opens, controls say *"Preparing… Please try again later"* | `com.samsung.tv.home.sidebar` or `contentservicemanager` missing |
| Home key does nothing / blank screen | the configured home app (`FreeMyTVio.*`) is missing or killed |
| App screen or inputs empty | `com.samsung.tv.csfs` / `tv-viewer` touched |
| Root acquisition fails, nothing applies | `sdbd` masked or down, or the exploit ran too early |

## Rules

1. **Do not hunt logs.** This firmware has none (`journalctl`, `dlogutil`, `/var/log/dlog` all empty).
2. **Bisect by restoring, newest-first.** Restore the most recent change in halves; wait for the human's
   confirmation between cycles.
3. **Restore + reboot + verify**, then re-run `./agent/audit.sh` so the next agent sees the truth.
4. **Check for a stale session before blaming a cut.** A DRM-style error can survive the TV's own reboot
   and clear only on a cold boot (power off, power on). If playback worked minutes earlier with the same
   config, suspect the session, not the config.

## Fast restore

```bash
BK=/opt/usr/share/tv-root-backups/<change-set>
mv $BK/<pkg> /opt/usr/apps/                      # directory back
# records back
sqlite3 /opt/dbspace/.pkgmgr_parser.db < /tmp/restore.sql   # app_disable='false', app_autorestart='true'
# and drop the pattern from /etc/tv-root-kill-procs, then:
tv run 'sync; reboot'
```

Masked unit: remove the line from `/etc/tv-root-perf-units`, then `tv svc unmask <unit>` (or reboot —
runtime masks clear themselves).

## After the fix

Record it: which piece, which symptom, found by which boot. Add it to `manifest.json → invariants` so the
next agent does not repeat the experiment. This is how `aaa_tvs_deamon` and the quick-settings pair got
documented — a wrong guess costs a reboot cycle, a written-down finding costs nothing.

## reclaim-memory

# Playbook — measure, then reclaim memory or boot time

## Measure first (idle only)

A streaming TV holds ~300 MB more than an idle one, so every reading must be idle-to-idle.

```bash
./agent/audit.sh | python3 -c 'import json,sys; d=json.load(sys.stdin); print(d["state"]["memory"], d["tv"]["launcher_start_offset_s"])'
```

What to trust:

- **RAM available / swap / CMA** from `/proc/meminfo` — higher available, lower swap, higher `CmaFree` is
  the goal (CMA is what the video decoder needs; when it collapses, playback stutters).
- **Launcher start offset** from `/proc/<pid>/stat` field 22 — this is what a person feels. The REST API
  answering early means nothing: it can be up 100 s before the first picture.

## Where the memory actually is

Ranked by what was measured on this platform:

1. **Art Mode** — `art-app` + `home.art`, ~187 MB. Also early in the boot queue, so it delays the launcher.
2. **Samsung Home app** — `home.media`, ~112 MB (safe only with sidebar + contentservicemanager present).
3. **Quick-panel stack** — `home.sidebar` ~93 MB + `contentservicemanager` ~20 MB. **Required** for quick
   settings; do not remove.
4. **Long tail** — `vif`, `context-aware*`, `easysetup`, `tap-service`, `airplay`, `samsung-cloud`,
   ~120 MB combined.
5. **Services** — telemetry/promo/OTA units, ~60 MB and a shorter boot queue.

Core framework (`csfs` ~150 MB, `FreeMyTV` ~70 MB on this build) is not negotiable.

## Boot time

Boot delay is the *startup queue*, not memory. Services start serially and the launcher is near the end
(~134–150 s on this set). Removing things that start ahead of the launcher shortens it; removing late
services does not. Map the queue before promising an improvement:

```bash
tv run 'ps -eo pid=,rss=,comm= | ... '   # or read /proc/<pid>/stat field 22 for each app
```

## Reporting

Quote the four numbers (available, swap, CMA, processes) plus launcher offset, before and after, and say
plainly if the change did not move them. "Felt faster" is not a measurement; neither is "memory improved".
